Kevalañhi tattha sāvakabodhisattassa vasena paññā āgatā, idha mahābodhisattassa vasena karuṇūpāyakosallapubbaṅgamaṃ katvā vattabbā, ñāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ apāpetvā paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhiyaṃyeva vipassanā ṭhapetabbāti ayameva viseso. Evamettha paññāpāramiyā paṭipattikkamo veditabbo.

Here, the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of the divine-ear element, the knowledge of penetrating others' minds, the knowledge of recollecting past lives, the knowledge of the divine eye, the knowledge of understanding the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, and the knowledge of the future—these, along with their auxiliary factors, constitute the five mundane higher knowledges, known as the wisdom of development. Furthermore, there is the wisdom of development, both mundane and supramundane, to be cultivated by one who, having accumulated knowledge through study and inquiry concerning the fundamental phenomena classified as aggregates, sense bases, elements, faculties, truths, dependent origination, and so on, and being established in the two root purifications of virtue and mind, accomplishes the five purifications that form the body of the path: purification of view, purification by overcoming doubt, purification by knowledge and vision of what is and is not the path, purification by knowledge and vision of the way, and purification of knowledge and vision. The method for accomplishing these is explained in all its aspects in the Visuddhimagga (Visuddhi. 2.430ff.), along with the division of their objects, beginning with, “Here, a beginning yogi wishing to perform the various psychic transformations, such as being one and becoming many…” and, “The aggregates are the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.” Therefore, it should be understood according to the method explained there. The only difference is that there, wisdom is presented from the perspective of a disciple or a bodhisatta, whereas here, for the Great Bodhisatta, it must be taught with compassion and skillful means as its forerunners. Insight is to be established in the purification by knowledge and vision of the way, without reaching the purification of knowledge and vision. This is the sole distinction. Thus, the progression of practice for the perfection of wisdom should be understood in this way.

Tathā yasmā sammāsambodhiyā katābhinīhārena mahāsattena pāramiparipūraṇatthaṃ sabbakālaṃ yuttappayuttena bhavitabbaṃ ābaddhaparikaraṇena, tasmā kālena kālaṃ “ko nu kho ajja mayā puññasambhāro ñāṇasambhāro vā upacito, kiṃ vā mayā parahitaṃ kata”nti divase divase paccavekkhantena sattahitatthaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo. Sabbesampi sattānaṃ upakārāya attano pariggahabhūtaṃ vatthu kāye jīvite ca nirapekkhacittena ossajitabbaṃ. Yaṃ kiñci kammaṃ karoti kāyena vācāya vā, taṃ sabbaṃ sambodhiyaṃ [P 0.0318] ninnacitteneva kātabbaṃ, bodhiyā pariṇāmetabbaṃ. Uḷārehi ittarehi ca kāmehi vinivattacitteneva bhavitabbaṃ. Sabbāsupi itikattabbatāsu upāyakosallaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpetvāva paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

Furthermore, since the great being, who has made the resolve for perfect enlightenment, must always be diligent and engaged, with preparations made, for the sake of fulfilling the perfections, he should therefore, from time to time, reflect daily: “What accumulation of merit or accumulation of wisdom have I generated today? What good have I done for others?” and make an effort for the welfare of beings. For the benefit of all beings, he should relinquish with a detached mind his own possessions, body, and life. Whatever action he performs, whether by body or speech, all should be done with a mind directed toward enlightenment and dedicated to enlightenment. He must have a mind turned away from both coarse and refined sensual pleasures. In all duties, he should proceed only after establishing skill in means.

Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sattahite āraddhavīriyena bhavitabbaṃ iṭṭhāniṭṭhādisabbasahena avisaṃvādinā. Sabbepi sattā anodhiso mettāya karuṇāya ca pharitabbā. Yā kāci sattānaṃ dukkhuppatti, sabbā sā attani pāṭikaṅkhitabbā. Sabbesañca sattānaṃ puññaṃ abbhanumoditabbaṃ. Buddhānaṃ mahantatā mahānubhāvatā abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbā. Yañca kiñci kammaṃ karoti kāyena vācāya vā, taṃ sabbaṃ bodhininnacittapubbaṅgamaṃ kātabbaṃ. Iminā hi upāyena dānādīsu yuttappayuttassa thāmavato daḷhaparakkamassa mahāsattassa bodhisattassa aparimeyyo puññasambhāro ñāṇasambhāro ca divase divase upacīyati.

In each and every act for the welfare of beings, one must be energetic, enduring all things pleasant, unpleasant, and so on, and be truthful. All beings should be suffused with boundless loving-kindness and compassion. Whatever suffering arises in any being, all of it should be regarded as one's own. And one should rejoice in the merit of all beings. The greatness and mighty power of the Buddhas should be frequently contemplated. Whatever action one performs, whether by body or speech, all should be preceded by a mind directed towards enlightenment. By this means, for the great being—the Bodhisatta—who is engaged in giving and other virtues, powerful, and firm in effort, an immeasurable accumulation of merit and wisdom grows day by day.

Api ca sattānaṃ paribhogatthaṃ paripālanatthañca attano sarīraṃ jīvitañca pariccajitvā khuppipāsāsītuṇhavātātapādidukkhapatikāro [V 0.0288] pariyesitabbo upanetabbo ca. Yañca yathāvuttadukkhapatikārajaṃ sukhaṃ attanā paṭilabhati, tathā ramaṇīyesu ārāmuyyānapāsādataḷākādīsu araññāyatanesu ca kāyacittasantāpābhāvena abhinibbutattā attanā [M 0.0310] sukhaṃ paṭilabhati, yañca suṇāti buddhānubuddhapaccekabuddhā mahābodhisattā ca nekkhammapaṭipattiyaṃ ṭhitā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārabhūtaṃ īdisaṃ nāma jhānasamāpattisukhaṃ anubhavantīti, taṃ sabbaṃ sabbasattesu anodhiso upasaṃharatīti. Ayaṃ tāva nayo asamāhitabhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhitassa.

Moreover, for the sake of beings' enjoyment and protection, having relinquished one's own body and life, one should seek and provide relief from the suffering of hunger, thirst, cold, heat, wind, sun, and the like. And whatever happiness one obtains by oneself from the relief of such suffering as described; and likewise the happiness one obtains by oneself in delightful parks, gardens, mansions, ponds, and forest hermitages, being at peace through the absence of bodily and mental distress; and whatever one hears, that the Buddhas, their disciples, the Paccekabuddhas, and the great bodhisattas, established in the practice of renunciation, experience such happiness of jhāna and attainments, which constitutes a blissful abiding in this very life—all of that one should impartially extend to all beings. This, for now, is the method for one established in the stage of non-concentration.

Samāhitabhūmiyaṃ pana patiṭṭhito attanā yathānubhūtaṃ visesādhigamanibbattaṃ pītiṃ passaddhiṃ sukhaṃ samādhiṃ yathābhūtañāṇañca sattesu adhimuccanto upasaṃharati pariṇāmeti. Tathā mahati saṃsāradukkhe tassa ca nimittabhūte kilesābhisaṅkhāradukkhe nimuggaṃ sattanikāyaṃ disvā tatrāpi chedanabhedanaphālanapiṃsanaggisantāpādijanitā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā nirantaraṃ cirakālaṃ vediyante nārake, aññamaññaṃ kujjhanasantāpanaviheṭhanahiṃsanaparādhīnatādīhi mahādukkhaṃ anubhavante tiracchānagate, jotimālākulasarīre khuppipāsāvātātapādīhi ḍayhamāne [P 0.0319] ca visussamāne ca vantakheḷādiāhāre uddhabāhuṃ viravante nijjhāmataṇhikādike mahādukkhaṃ vediyamāne pete ca, pariyeṭṭhimūlakaṃ mahantaṃ anayabyasanaṃ pāpuṇante hatthacchedādikāraṇāyogena dubbaṇṇaduddasikadaliddādibhāvena khuppipāsādiābādhayogena balavantehi abhibhavanīyato paresaṃ vahanato parādhīnato ca, nārake pete tiracchānagate ca, atisayante apāyadukkhanibbisesaṃ dukkhamanubhavante manusse ca, tathā visayavisaparibhogavikkhittacittatāya rāgādipariḷāhena ḍayhamāne vātavegasamuṭṭhitajālāsamiddhasukkhakaṭṭhasannipāte aggikkhandhe viya anupasantapariḷāhavuttike anupasantanihataparādhīne kāmāvacaradeve ca, mahatā vāyāmena vidūramākāsaṃ vigāhitasakuntā viya balavatā dūre pāṇinā khittasarā viya ca, satipi cirappavattiyaṃ aniccantikatāya pātapariyosānā anatikkantajātijarāmaraṇā evāti rūpārūpāvacaradeve ca passantena mahantaṃ saṃvegaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā mettāya karuṇāya ca anodhiso sattā pharitabbā. Evaṃ kāyena vācāya manasā ca bodhisambhāre nirantaraṃ upacinantena yathā pāramiyo pāripūriṃ gacchanti, evaṃ sakkaccakārinā sātaccakārinā anolīnavuttinā ussāho pavattetabbo, vīriyapāramī paripūretabbā.

One who is established in the stage of concentration, however, being intent upon them, applies to beings and dedicates the joy, tranquility, happiness, concentration, and knowledge of things as they truly are—realized through personal attainment of distinction. Likewise, seeing the host of beings submerged in the great suffering of saṃsāra and in the suffering of defilements and formations, which are its cause—and in hell, enduring continuous, long-lasting, intense, harsh, and bitter feelings born of being cut, split, pierced, crushed, and burned with fire; and in the animal realm, experiencing great suffering through mutual anger, torment, harassment, harm, and dependence on others; and among hungry ghosts, with bodies ablaze, being burned and withered by hunger, thirst, wind, and heat, screaming with upraised arms for food such as vomit and spittle, enduring the great suffering of being consumed by hunger and thirst; and among humans, encountering great misfortune and calamity rooted in seeking, due to causes such as being maimed, becoming ugly, repulsive, and poor, due to afflictions like hunger and thirst, being overpowered by the strong, carrying burdens for others, and being dependent on others; and in hell, among hungry ghosts, and in the animal realm; and among humans, experiencing suffering that surpasses and is indistinguishable from the suffering of the lower realms; and among the devas of the sense sphere, their minds distracted by enjoying the poison of sense objects, burning with the fever of passion, like a great mass of fire with unquenched flames in a pile of dry wood stirred by the wind's force, their feverish existence unpacified, themselves unpacified, oppressed, and dependent; and among the devas of the form and formless realms, like birds that have flown far into the distant sky with great effort or arrows shot far by a strong arm, seeing that even their long-lasting existence ends in falling due to impermanence, not having transcended birth, aging, and death—one establishes great spiritual urgency. With loving-kindness and compassion, one should pervade beings without limit. Thus, one who continuously accumulates the requisites of enlightenment—through body, speech, and mind—so that the perfections are fulfilled, should generate effort, acting diligently, constantly, and with unflagging conduct. The perfection of energy should be fully developed.

Api [M 0.0311] ca acinteyyāparimeyyavipuloḷāravimalanirupamanirūpakkilesaguṇanicayanidhānabhūtassa buddhabhāvassa ussakkitvā sampahaṃsanayoggaṃ vīriyaṃ nāma acinteyyānubhāvameva, yaṃ na pacurajanā [V 0.0289] sotumpi sakkuṇanti, pageva paṭipajjituṃ. Tathā hi tividhā abhinīhāracittuppatti, catasso buddhabhūmiyo, cattāri saṅgahavatthūni, karuṇekarasatā, buddhadhammesu sacchikaraṇena visesappaccayo nijjhānakhanti, sabbadhammesu nirupalepo, sabbasattesu piyaputtasaññā, saṃsāradukkhehi aparikhedo, sabbadeyyadhammapariccāgo, tena ca niratimānatā, adhisīlādiadhiṭṭhānaṃ, tattha ca acañcalatā, kusalakiriyāsu pītipāmojjaṃ, vivekaninnacittatā, jhānānuyogo, anavajjadhammena atitti, yathāsutassa dhammassa paresaṃ hitajjhāsayena desanā, sattānaṃ ñāye nivesanā, ārambhadaḷhatā, dhīravīrabhāvo, parāpavādaparāpakāresu vikārābhāvo, saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ, samāpattīsu [P 0.0320] vasībhāvo, abhiññāsu balappatti, lakkhaṇattayāvabodho, satipaṭṭhānādīsu yogakammābhiyogena lokuttaramaggasambhārasambharaṇaṃ, navalokuttarāvakkantīti evamādikā sabbāpi bodhisambhārapaṭipatti vīriyānubhāveneva samijjhatīti abhinīhārato yāva mahābodhi anossajjantena sakkaccaṃ nirantaraṃ vīriyaṃ yathā uparūpari visesāvahaṃ hoti, evaṃ sampādetabbaṃ. Sampajjamāne ca yathāvutte vīriye khantisaccādhiṭṭhānādayo ca dānasīlādayo ca sabbepi bodhisambhārā tadadhīnavuttitāya sampannā eva hontīti khantiādīsupi imināva nayena paṭipatti veditabbā.

Moreover, the effort that is worthy of being extolled and praised, pertaining to the state of Buddhahood—which is inconceivable, immeasurable, vast, extensive, stainless, incomparable, free from defilements, and the foundation of all virtues—is indeed of inconceivable power, which most people cannot even hear about, let alone practice. For instance, the threefold arising of the thought of aspiration; the four Buddha-stages; the four bases of beneficence; compassion as the sole essence; the special condition of conviction through the realization of the Buddha's teachings; non-adherence to all phenomena; the perception of all beings as dear children; non-weariness with the sufferings of saṃsāra; the relinquishment of all things to be given, and absence of conceit thereby; the determination for higher virtue and so forth, and unshakeability therein; joy and gladness in wholesome actions; a mind inclined to seclusion; dedication to meditation; insatiability with blameless qualities; teaching the Dhamma as heard to others with the intention of their welfare; establishing beings in the right method; firmness in undertaking; the state of being a wise hero; absence of alteration in the face of others' blame or harm; determination of truth; mastery in attainments; attainment of power in the higher knowledges; comprehension of the three characteristics; the accumulation of the requisites for the supramundane path through diligent application of the practice of mindfulness foundations and so forth; and the descent into the nine supramundane states—all such practices of the requisites of enlightenment succeed through the power of effort. Thus, from the aspiration up to the great enlightenment, one must diligently and continuously cultivate effort without abandoning it, so that it brings about higher and higher distinctions. And when the aforesaid effort is accomplished, then patience, determination of truth, and so forth, and generosity, virtue, and so forth, all the requisites of enlightenment, are fulfilled because their existence is dependent on it. The practice of patience and so forth should also be understood in the same way by this method.

Iti sattānaṃ sukhūpakaraṇapariccāgena bahudhā anuggahakaraṇaṃ dānena paṭipatti, sīlena tesaṃ jīvitasāpateyyadārarakkhāabhedapiyahitavacanāvihiṃsādikāraṇāni, nekkhammena tesaṃ āmisapaṭiggahaṇadhammadānādinā anekavidhā hitacariyā, paññāya tesaṃ hitakaraṇūpāyakosallaṃ, vīriyena tattha ussāhārambhaasaṃhīrāni, khantiyā tadaparādhasahanaṃ, saccena nesaṃ avañcanatadupakārakiriyāsamādānāvisaṃvādanādi, adhiṭṭhānena tadupakārakaraṇe anatthasampātepi acalanaṃ, mettāya nesaṃ hitasukhānucintanaṃ, upekkhāya nesaṃ upakārāpakāresu vikārānāpattīti evaṃ aparimāṇe satte ārabbha anukampitasabbasattassa mahābodhisattassa [M 0.0312] puthujjanehi asādhāraṇo aparimeyyo puññañāṇasambhārūpacayo ettha paṭipattīti veditabbaṃ. Yo cetāsaṃ paccayo vutto, tassa ca sakkaccaṃ sampādanaṃ.

Thus, the practice through generosity is benefiting beings in many ways by relinquishing things conducive to their happiness. Through virtue, it is the protection of their lives, property, and wives; the causes of non-divisive, endearing, and beneficial speech, non-violence, and so forth. Through renunciation, it is various kinds of beneficial conduct for them, such as the acceptance of material things and the giving of Dhamma, and so forth. Through wisdom, it is the skill in means for their welfare. Through energy, it is the undertaking of exertion and non-faltering therein. Through patience, it is the endurance of their offenses. Through truth, it is non-deception of them, undertaking beneficial actions for them, faithfulness to one's word, and so forth. Through determination, it is unshakeability in performing beneficial actions for them, even when misfortune befalls. Through loving-kindness, it is the contemplation of their welfare and happiness. Through equanimity, it is the non-occurrence of alteration regarding their help or harm. In this way, with reference to immeasurable beings, the great Bodhisattva, who has compassion for all beings, accumulates an immeasurable collection of merit and knowledge, which is uncommon among ordinary people. This is to be understood as the practice here. And that which has been stated as the cause of these practices is to be diligently accomplished.

Ko vibhāgoti? Dasa pāramiyo, dasa upapāramiyo, dasa paramatthapāramiyoti samattiṃsapāramiyo. Tattha katābhinīhārassa bodhisattassa parahitakaraṇābhininnāsayapayogassa kaṇhadhammavokiṇṇā sukkadhammā pāramiyo eva, tehi avokiṇṇā sukkadhammā upapāramiyo, akaṇhaasukkā paramatthapāramiyoti keci. Samudāgamanakālesu vā pūriyamānā pāramiyo, bodhisattabhūmiyaṃ puṇṇā upapāramiyo, buddhabhūmiyaṃ sabbākāraparipuṇṇā paramatthapāramiyo. Bodhisattabhūmiyaṃ [V 0.0290] vā parahitakaraṇato pāramiyo, attahitakaraṇato upapāramiyo, buddhabhūmiyaṃ balavesārajjasamadhigamena ubhayahitaparipūraṇato paramatthapāramiyo.

What is the classification? There are ten perfections, ten secondary perfections, and ten ultimate perfections—thirty perfections in total. Among these, according to some, for a Bodhisatta who has made an aspiration and is inclined to and striving for the welfare of others, the perfections are the bright qualities mixed with dark qualities; the secondary perfections are the bright qualities unmixed with those; and qualities that are neither dark nor bright are the ultimate perfections. Alternatively, the perfections are those being fulfilled at the times of their arising; the secondary perfections are those fulfilled in the Bodhisatta stage; and the ultimate perfections are those completely perfected in every way in the Buddha stage. Or, in the Bodhisatta stage, those qualities leading to the welfare of others are the perfections; those for one's own welfare are the secondary perfections; and in the Buddha stage, through the attainment of powers and intrepidity, the perfect fulfillment of both welfares constitutes the ultimate perfections.

Evaṃ ādimajjhapariyosānesu paṇidhānārambhapariniṭṭhānesu tesaṃ vibhāgoti apare. Dosūpasamakaruṇāpakatikānaṃ bhavasukhavimuttisukhaparamasukhappattānaṃ [P 0.0321] puññūpacayabhedato tabbibhāgoti aññe. Lajjāsatimānāpassayānaṃ lokuttaradhammādhipatīnaṃ sīlasamādhipaññāgarukānaṃ tāritataritatārayitūnaṃ anubuddhapaccekabuddhasammāsambuddhānaṃ pāramī, upapāramī, paramatthapāramīti bodhisattassuppattito yathāvuttavibhāgoti keci. Cittapaṇidhito yāva vacīpaṇidhi, tāva pavattā sambhārā pāramiyo, vacīpaṇidhito yāva kāyapaṇidhi, tāva pavattā upapāramiyo, kāyapaṇidhito pabhuti paramatthapāramiyoti apare. Aññe pana “parapuññānumodanavasena pavattā sambhārā pāramiyo, paresaṃ kārāpanavasena pavattā upapāramiyo, sayaṃkaraṇavasena pavattā paramatthapāramiyo”ti vadanti.

Thus, others classify them according to the beginning, middle, and end, in the stages of aspiration, commencement, and completion. Still others say their classification is based on the difference in the accumulation of merit of those who have subdued aversion, are compassionate by nature, and have attained the happiness of existence, the happiness of liberation, and supreme happiness. Some say that for those who possess moral shame, mindfulness, and self-respect, who are masters of the supramundane Dhamma, who value virtue, concentration, and wisdom, and who have crossed over, been led across, and lead others across—that is, for Anubuddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and Sammāsambuddhas—the classification is as pāramī, upapāramī, and paramatthapāramī, a classification that some say is as stated, based on the arising of the Bodhisatta. Others say: 'From the aspiration of the mind until the aspiration of speech, the accumulated requisites are the perfections; from the aspiration of speech until the aspiration of the body, they are the secondary perfections; from the aspiration of the body onwards, they are the ultimate perfections.' Yet others declare: 'The accumulated requisites that arise through rejoicing in the merit of others are the perfections; those that arise through causing others to act are the secondary perfections; those that arise through one's own actions are the ultimate perfections.'

Tathā bhavasukhāvaho puññañāṇasambhāro pāramī, attano nibbānasukhāvaho upapāramī, paresaṃ tadubhayasukhāvaho paramatthapāramīti eke. Puttadāradhanādiupakaraṇapariccāgo pana dānapāramī, aṅgapariccāgo dānaupapāramī, attano jīvitapariccāgo dānaparamatthapāramīti. Tathā puttadārādikassa tividhassāpi hetu avītikkamanavasena tisso sīlapāramiyo, tesu eva tividhesu vatthūsu ālayaṃ upacchinditvā nikkhamanavasena [M 0.0313] tisso nekkhammapāramiyo, upakaraṇaṅgajīvitataṇhaṃ samūhanitvā sattānaṃ hitāhitavinicchayakaraṇavasena tisso paññāpāramiyo. Yathāvuttabhedānaṃ pariccāgādīnaṃ vāyamanavasena tisso vīriyapāramiyo, upakaraṇaṅgajīvitantarāyakarānaṃ khamanavasena tisso khantipāramiyo, upakaraṇaṅgajīvitahetu saccāpariccāgavasena tisso saccapāramiyo, dānādipāramiyo akuppādhiṭṭhānavaseneva samijjhantīti, upakaraṇādivināsepi acalādhiṭṭhānavasena tisso adhiṭṭhānapāramiyo, upakaraṇādiupaghātakesupi sattesu mettāya avijahanavasena tisso mettāpāramiyo, yathāvuttavatthuttayassa upakārāpakāresu sattasaṅkhāresu majjhattatāpaṭilābhavasena tisso upekkhāpāramiyoti evamādinā etāsaṃ vibhāgo veditabbāti.

Thus, some say that the accumulation of merit and knowledge that brings happiness in existence is the perfection; that which brings the happiness of one's own Nibbāna is the secondary perfection; and that which brings both kinds of happiness to others is the ultimate perfection. The relinquishment of possessions such as children, spouse, and wealth is the perfection of generosity; the relinquishment of limbs is the secondary perfection of generosity; the relinquishment of one's own life is the ultimate perfection of generosity. Similarly, the three perfections of virtue are by way of non-transgression regarding the threefold basis of children, spouse, and so forth. The three perfections of renunciation are by way of abandoning attachment and departing from those same threefold objects. The three perfections of wisdom are by way of uprooting craving for possessions, limbs, and life, and by discerning what is beneficial and harmful for beings. The three perfections of energy are by way of exertion in the relinquishments and so forth, as described. The three perfections of patience are by way of enduring those who cause danger to possessions, limbs, and life. The three perfections of truth are by way of not relinquishing truth for the sake of possessions, limbs, and life. The perfections such as generosity succeed only by way of unwavering determination. Thus, the three perfections of determination are by way of unshakeable determination even in the destruction of possessions and so forth. The three perfections of loving-kindness are by way of not abandoning loving-kindness even toward beings who harm possessions and so forth. The three perfections of equanimity are by way of attaining neutrality toward helpful and harmful beings and formations with respect to the aforementioned threefold object. In this way, the classification of these perfections should be understood.

Ko saṅgahoti? Ettha pana yathā etā vibhāgato tiṃsavidhāpi dānapāramiādibhāvato dasavidhā, evaṃ dānasīlakhantivīriyajhānapaññāsabhāvena chabbidhā. Etāsu hi nekkhammapāramī sīlapāramiyā saṅgahitā, tassā pabbajjābhāve, nīvaraṇavivekabhāve pana jhānapāramiyā kusaladhammabhāve [V 0.0291] chahipi saṅgahitā. Saccapāramī sīlapāramiyā [P 0.0322] ekadeso eva vacīviratisaccapakkhe, ñāṇasaccapakkhe pana paññāpāramiyā saṅgahitā. Mettāpārami jhānapāramiyā eva. Upekkhāpāramī jhānapaññāpāramīhi. Adhiṭṭhānapāramī sabbāhipi saṅgahitāti.

What is the inclusion? Here, just as these, though thirtyfold in division, are tenfold in terms of the nature of the perfections of giving and so on, so too they are sixfold by way of the nature of giving, virtue, patience, energy, absorption, and wisdom. Among these, the perfection of renunciation is included in the perfection of virtue in its aspect of going forth; but in its aspect of seclusion from hindrances, it is included in the perfection of absorption; and in its aspect of wholesome qualities, it is included in all six. The perfection of truth is merely a part of the perfection of virtue, specifically in the aspect of truth as verbal abstinence, but in the aspect of truth as knowledge, it is included in the perfection of wisdom. The perfection of loving-kindness is included in the perfection of absorption. The perfection of equanimity is included in the perfections of absorption and wisdom. The perfection of determination is included in all of them.

Etesañca dānādīnaṃ channaṃ guṇānaṃ aññamaññasambandhānaṃ pañcadasayugalādīni pañcadasayugalādisādhakāni honti. Seyyathidaṃ – dānasīlayugalena parahitāhitānaṃ karaṇākaraṇayugalasiddhi, dānakhantiyugalena alobhādosayugalasiddhi, dānavīriyayugalena cāgasutayugalasiddhi, dānajhānayugalena kāmadosappahānayugalasiddhi. Dānapaññāyugalena ariyayānadhurayugalasiddhi, sīlakhantidvayena payogāsayasuddhidvayasiddhi, sīlavīriyadvayena bhāvanādvayasiddhi, sīlajhānadvayena dussīlyapariyuṭṭhānappahānadvayasiddhi, sīlapaññādvayena dānadvayasiddhi, khantivīriyayugalena khamātejadvayasiddhi, khantijhānayugalena virodhānurodhappahānayugalasiddhi, khantipaññāyugalena suññatākhantipaṭivedhadukasiddhi, vīriyajhānadukena paggahāvikkhepadukasiddhi, vīriyapaññādukena saraṇadukasiddhi, jhānapaññādukena yānadukasiddhi[M 0.0314], dānasīlakhantittikena lobhadosamohappahānattikasiddhi, dānasīlavīriyattikena bhogajīvitakāyasārādānattikasiddhi, dānasīlajhānattikena puññakiriyavatthuttikasiddhi, dānasīlapaññātikena āmisābhayadhammadānattikasiddhīti. Evaṃ itarehipi tikehi catukkādīhi ca yathāsambhavaṃ tikāni ca catukkādīni ca yojetabbāni.

And these six qualities, beginning with giving, being interrelated, are what accomplish the fifteen pairs and so on. Namely: The pair of giving and virtue accomplishes the pair of doing and not doing what is beneficial and harmful to others. The pair of giving and patience accomplishes the pair of non-greed and non-aversion. The pair of giving and effort accomplishes the pair of generosity and erudition. The pair of giving and meditation accomplishes the pair of abandoning sensual desire and aversion. The pair of giving and wisdom accomplishes the pair of bearing the yoke of the noble vehicle. The pair of virtue and patience accomplishes the pair of purity of exertion and intention. The pair of virtue and effort accomplishes the pair of the two developments. The pair of virtue and meditation accomplishes the pair of abandoning misconduct and obsessive defilements. The pair of virtue and wisdom accomplishes the pair of the two givings. The pair of patience and effort accomplishes the pair of forbearance and energy. The pair of patience and meditation accomplishes the pair of abandoning opposition and conformity. The pair of patience and wisdom accomplishes the pair of acceptance of emptiness and its penetration. The pair of effort and meditation accomplishes the pair of exertion and non-distraction. The pair of effort and wisdom accomplishes the pair of the two refuges. The pair of meditation and wisdom accomplishes the pair of the two vehicles. The triad of giving, virtue, and patience accomplishes the triad of abandoning greed, aversion, and delusion. The triad of giving, virtue, and effort accomplishes the triad of taking the essence of wealth, life, and the body. The triad of giving, virtue, and meditation accomplishes the triad of bases for meritorious action. The triad of giving, virtue, and wisdom accomplishes the triad of material gifts, gifts of fearlessness, and Dhamma gifts. In this way, the remaining triads, tetrads, and so on should be connected as is suitable.

Evaṃ chabbidhānampi pana imāsaṃ pāramīnaṃ catūhi adhiṭṭhānehi saṅgaho veditabbo. Sabbapāramīnaṃ samūhasaṅgahato hi cattāri adhiṭṭhānāni, seyyathidaṃ – saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ, cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ, upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ, paññādhiṭṭhānanti. Tattha adhitiṭṭhati etena, ettha vā adhitiṭṭhati, adhiṭṭhānamattameva vā tanti adhiṭṭhānaṃ, saccañca taṃ adhiṭṭhānañca, saccassa vā adhiṭṭhānaṃ, saccaṃ adhiṭṭhānametassāti vā saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Evaṃ sesesupi. Tattha avisesato tāva lokuttaraguṇe katābhinīhārassa anukampitasabbasattassa mahāsattassa paṭiññānurūpaṃ sabbapāramipariggahato saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tāsaṃ paṭipakkhapariccāgato cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ[P 0.0323]. Sabbapāramitāguṇehi upasamato upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tehi eva parahitopāyakosallato paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ.

Thus, these sixfold perfections should be understood as grouped by four foundations. For from the collective grouping of all perfections there are four foundations, namely: the foundation of truth, the foundation of relinquishment, the foundation of tranquility, and the foundation of wisdom. Herein, 'foundation' is that by which one stands firm, or in which one stands firm, or it is merely the act of standing firm. 'The foundation of truth' is the truth which is a foundation, or the foundation of truth, or that for which truth is the foundation. The same applies to the rest. Here, first of all, in a general sense, for the Great Being who has resolved upon supramundane qualities and who has compassion for all beings, the foundation of truth is from embracing all perfections in accordance with his vow. The foundation of relinquishment is from relinquishing their opposing factors. The foundation of tranquility is from being calmed by all the qualities of the perfections. The foundation of wisdom is from the skill in means for the welfare of others through these very qualities.

Visesato pana yācakajanaṃ avisaṃvādetvā dassāmīti paṭijānanato paṭiññaṃ avisaṃvādetvā [V 0.0292] dānato dānaṃ avisaṃvādetvā anumodanato macchariyādipaṭipakkhapariccāgato deyyadhammapaṭiggāhakadānadeyyadhammakkhayesu lobhadosamohabhayavūpasamato yathārahaṃ yathākālaṃ yathāvidhānañca dānato paññuttarato ca kusaladhammānaṃ caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ dānaṃ. Tathā saṃvarasamādānassa avītikkamanato dussīlyapariccāgato duccaritavūpasamanato paññuttarato ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ sīlaṃ. Yathāpaṭiññaṃ khamanato, parāparādhavikappapariccāgato, kodhapariyuṭṭhānavūpasamanato, paññuttarato, ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānā khanti. Paṭiññānurūpaṃ parahitakaraṇato, visadapariccāgato, akusalavūpasamanato, paññuttarato ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ vīriyaṃ. Paṭiññānurūpaṃ lokahitānucintanato, nīvaraṇapariccāgato, cittavūpasamanato, paññuttarato ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ jhānaṃ. Yathāpaṭiññaṃ parahitūpāyakosallato, anupāyakiriyāpariccāgato, mohajapariḷāhavūpasamanato, sabbaññutāpaṭilābhato ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānā paññā.

Specifically, giving has its basis in the four foundations: in truth, through promising 'I will give' without deceiving those who ask, giving without breaking that promise, and rejoicing in giving without deceit; in relinquishment, through relinquishing stinginess and other opposing factors; in tranquility, through pacifying greed, aversion, delusion, and fear concerning the gift, the recipient, the giver, and the exhaustion of the gift; and in wisdom, through giving as is suitable, at the right time, and in the right way, and through its wholesome qualities being led by wisdom. Similarly, virtue has its basis in the four foundations: in truth, through not transgressing the undertaking of restraint; in relinquishment, through relinquishing immorality; in tranquility, through pacifying misconduct; and in wisdom, through being led by it. Patience has its basis in the four foundations: in truth, through enduring according to one's promise; in relinquishment, through relinquishing thoughts of others' offenses; in tranquility, through pacifying the obsession of anger; and in wisdom, through being led by it. Effort has its basis in the four foundations: in truth, through acting for the welfare of others in accordance with one's promise; in relinquishment, through relinquishing dejection; in tranquility, through pacifying unwholesome states; and in wisdom, through being led by it. Meditation has its basis in the four foundations: in truth, through contemplating the welfare of the world in line with one's promise; in relinquishment, through relinquishing the hindrances; in tranquility, through pacifying the mind; and in wisdom, through being led by it. Wisdom has its basis in the four foundations: in truth, through skill in means for the welfare of others according to one's promise; in relinquishment, through relinquishing action that is not a proper means; in tranquility, through pacifying the fever born of delusion; and in wisdom, through the attainment of omniscience.

Tattha [M 0.0315] ñeyyapaṭiññānuvidhānehi saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Vatthukāmakilesakāmapariccāgehi cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Dosadukkhavūpasamehi upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Anubodhapaṭivedhehi paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tividhasaccapariggahitaṃ dosattayavirodhi saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tividhacāgapariggahitaṃ dosattayavirodhi cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tividhavūpasamapariggahitaṃ dosattayavirodhi upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tividhañāṇapariggahitaṃ dosattayavirodhi paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Saccādhiṭṭhānapariggahitāni cāgūpasamapaññādhiṭṭhānāni avisaṃvādanato paṭiññānuvidhānato ca, cāgādhiṭṭhānapariggahitāni saccūpasamapaññādhiṭṭhānāni paṭipakkhapariccāgato sabbapariccāgaphalattā ca, upasamādhiṭṭhānapariggahitāni saccacāgapaññādhiṭṭhānāni kilesapariḷāhavūpasamanato kāmūpasamanato kāmapariḷāhavūpasamanato ca, paññādhiṭṭhānapariggahitāni saccacāgūpasamādhiṭṭhānāni ñāṇapubbaṅgamato ñāṇānuparivattanato cāti evaṃ sabbāpi pāramiyo saccappabhāvitā cāgaparibyañjitā upasamopabrūhitā [P 0.0324] paññāparisuddhā. Saccañhi etāsaṃ janakahetu. Cāgo pariggāhakahetu, upasamo parivuddhihetu, paññā pārisuddhihetu. Tathā ādimhi saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ saccapaṭiññattā, majjhe cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ katapaṇidhānassa parahitāya attapariccāgato. Ante upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ sabbūpasamapariyosānattā. Ādimajjhapariyosānesu paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ tasmiṃ sati sambhavato asati abhāvato yathāpaṭiññañca bhāvato.

Here, the foundation of truth is through conformity with the acknowledgment of what is to be known. The foundation of relinquishment is through the abandonment of sensual objects and sensual defilements. The foundation of peace is through the subsiding of aversion and suffering. The foundation of wisdom is through understanding and penetration. The foundation of truth, embraced by the threefold truth, opposes the three defilements. The foundation of relinquishment, embraced by the threefold relinquishment, opposes the three defilements. The foundation of peace, embraced by the threefold peace, opposes the three defilements. The foundation of wisdom, embraced by the threefold knowledge, opposes the three defilements. The foundations of relinquishment, peace, and wisdom, embraced by the foundation of truth, are so by reason of non-deception and conformity with acknowledgment. The foundations of truth, peace, and wisdom, embraced by the foundation of relinquishment, are so by reason of abandoning opposition and because of resulting in the fruit of all relinquishment. The foundations of truth, relinquishment, and wisdom, embraced by the foundation of peace, are so by reason of the subsiding of the burning of defilements, the subsiding of sensual desire, and the subsiding of the burning of sensual desire. The foundations of truth, relinquishment, and peace, embraced by the foundation of wisdom, are so by reason of wisdom being the forerunner and because of revolving in accordance with wisdom. Thus, all the perfections are illumined by truth, distinguished by relinquishment, strengthened by peace, and purified by wisdom. For truth is their generating cause. Relinquishment is their embracing cause, peace is their nurturing cause, and wisdom is their purifying cause. Likewise, in the beginning is the foundation of truth, because of the declaration of truth; in the middle is the foundation of relinquishment, because of the sacrifice of self for the good of others by one who has made a vow; at the end is the foundation of peace, because of culminating in all peace. In the beginning, middle, and end is the foundation of wisdom, because when it exists, it arises; when it does not exist, it is absent; and because of developing in accordance with the declaration.

Tattha mahāpurisā satatamattahitaparahitakarehi garupiyabhāvakarehi saccacāgādhiṭṭhānehi gihibhūtā [V 0.0293] āmisadānena pare anuggaṇhanti. Tathā attahitaparahitakarehi garupiyabhāvakarehi upasamapaññādhiṭṭhānehi ca pabbajitabhūtā dhammadānena pare anuggaṇhanti.

There, great beings, constantly engaged in actions beneficial to themselves and others, inspiring reverence and affection, established in the foundations of truth and relinquishment, as householders, assist others with material gifts. Likewise, those engaged in actions beneficial to themselves and others, inspiring reverence and affection, established in the foundations of peace and wisdom, as renunciants, assist others with the gift of the Dhamma.

Tattha antimabhave bodhisattassa caturadhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇaṃ. Paripuṇṇacaturadhiṭṭhānassa hi carimakabhavūpapattīti eke. Tatra hi gabbhokkantiṭhitiabhinikkhamanesu paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena sato sampajāno saccādhiṭṭhānapāripūriyā sampatijāto uttarābhimukho sattapadavītihārena gantvā sabbā disā oloketvā saccānuparivattinā vacasā – “aggohamasmi lokassa, jeṭṭhohamasmi lokassa, seṭṭhohamasmi lokassā”ti (dī. ni. 2.31; ma. ni. 3.207) tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadi.

In that final existence of the Bodhisatta, the fulfillment of the four foundations occurs. Some say that rebirth in the last existence is for one whose four foundations are fulfilled. There, at his conception, gestation, and birth, with the arising of the foundation of wisdom, he was mindful and clearly comprehending. Through the fulfillment of the foundation of truth, immediately after birth, facing north and taking seven steps, he surveyed all directions and with words that accord with truth, roared the lion's roar three times: 'I am the chief in the world, I am the eldest in the world, I am the best in the world.'

Upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena [M 0.0316] jiṇṇāturamatapabbajitadassāvino catudhammapadesakovidassa yobbanārogyajīvitasampattimadānaṃ upasamo. Cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena mahato ñātiparivaṭṭassa hatthagatassa ca cakkavattirajjassa anapekkhapariccāgoti.

Through the arising of the foundation of peace, for one who sees the old, the sick, the dead, and the renunciant, and is skilled in the four sights, there is the subsiding of the intoxication with the attainments of youth, health, and life. Through the arising of the foundation of relinquishment, there is the indifferent abandonment of a great circle of relatives and of the sovereignty of a wheel-turning monarch that was in his grasp.

Dutiye ṭhāne abhisambodhiyaṃ caturadhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti keci. Tattha hi yathāpaṭiññaṃ saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ abhisamayo, tato hi saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena sabbakilesūpakkilesapariccāgo, tato hi cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena paramūpasamappatti, tato hi upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena anāvaraṇañāṇapaṭilābho, tato hi paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti. Taṃ asiddhaṃ, abhisambodhiyāpi paramatthabhāvato.

In the second instance, some say the four foundations are fulfilled at enlightenment. There, through the arising of the foundation of truth in accordance with one’s promise, there is the realization of the four noble truths—thus, the foundation of truth is fulfilled. Through the arising of the foundation of relinquishment, there is the abandonment of all defilements and corruptions—thus, the foundation of relinquishment is fulfilled. Through the arising of the foundation of peace, there is the attainment of supreme peace—thus, the foundation of peace is fulfilled. Through the arising of the foundation of wisdom, there is the acquisition of unobstructed knowledge—thus, the foundation of wisdom is fulfilled. But that is not established, since enlightenment too is of ultimate reality.

Tatiye ṭhāne dhammacakkappavattane caturadhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti aññe. Tattha hi saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa dvādasahi ākārehi ariyasaccadesanāya [P 0.0325] saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa saddhammamahāyāgakaraṇena cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa sayaṃ upasantassa paresaṃ upasamanena upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa veneyyānaṃ āsayādiparijānanena paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti. Tadapi asiddhaṃ, apariyositattā buddhakiccassa.

In the third instance, others say the four foundations are fulfilled at the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma. There, for one who has attained the foundation of truth, the foundation of truth is fulfilled through the teaching of the Noble Truths in twelve aspects. For one who has attained the foundation of relinquishment, the foundation of relinquishment is fulfilled by performing the great sacrifice of the True Dhamma. For one who has attained the foundation of peace, being himself at peace, the foundation of peace is fulfilled by pacifying others. For one who has attained the foundation of wisdom, the foundation of wisdom is fulfilled by discerning the dispositions and so on of those to be trained. That too, however, is not established, because the Buddha's task was not yet concluded.

Catutthe ṭhāne parinibbāne caturadhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti apare. Tatra hi parinibbutattā paramatthasaccasampattiyā saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggena cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Sabbasaṅkhārūpasamena [V 0.0294] upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Paññāpayojanapariniṭṭhānena paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti. Tatra mahāpurisassa visesena mettākhette abhijātiyaṃ saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa saccādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇamabhibyattaṃ, visesena karuṇākhette abhisambodhiyaṃ paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa paññādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇamabhibyattaṃ, visesena muditākhette dhammacakkappavattane cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa cāgādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇamabhibyattaṃ, visesena upekkhākhette parinibbāne upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa upasamādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇamabhibyattanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In the fourth instance, still others say the four foundations are fulfilled at final Nibbāna. There, because of having attained final Nibbāna, the foundation of truth is fulfilled by the attainment of ultimate truth. Through the relinquishment of all substrata of existence, the foundation of relinquishment is fulfilled. Through the stilling of all formations, the foundation of peace is fulfilled. Through the culmination of the purpose of wisdom, the foundation of wisdom is fulfilled. Here, it should be understood that for the Great Being, the fulfillment of the foundation of truth, for one who has attained the foundation of truth, is especially manifest in the field of loving-kindness at his birth; the fulfillment of the foundation of wisdom, for one who has attained the foundation of wisdom, is especially manifest in the field of compassion at his full enlightenment; the fulfillment of the foundation of relinquishment, for one who has attained the foundation of relinquishment, is especially manifest in the field of sympathetic joy at the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma; and the fulfillment of the foundation of peace, for one who has attained the foundation of peace, is especially manifest in the field of equanimity at final Nibbāna.

Tatra [M 0.0317] saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa saṃvāsena sīlaṃ veditabbaṃ. Cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa saṃvohārena soceyyaṃ veditabbaṃ. Upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa āpadāsu thāmo veditabbo. Paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa sākacchāya paññā veditabbā. Evaṃ sīlājīvacittadiṭṭhivisuddhiyo veditabbā. Tathā saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena dosāgatiṃ na gacchati avisaṃvādanato. Cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena lobhāgatiṃ na gacchati anabhisaṅgato. Upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena bhayāgatiṃ na gacchati anaparādhato. Paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena mohāgatiṃ na gacchati yathā bhūtāvabodhato.

Here, for one who has attained the resolution of truth, virtue is to be known through living together. For one who has attained the resolution of relinquishment, purity is to be known through dealings. For one who has attained the resolution of tranquility, steadfastness is to be known in adversity. For one who has attained the resolution of wisdom, wisdom is to be known through discussion. Thus, the purities of virtue, livelihood, mind, and view are to be known. Furthermore, by attaining the resolution of truth, one does not fall into the wrong course of aversion, on account of truthfulness. By attaining the resolution of relinquishment, one does not fall into the wrong course of greed, on account of non-clinging. By attaining the resolution of tranquility, one does not fall into the wrong course of fear, on account of non-transgression. By attaining the resolution of wisdom, one does not fall into the wrong course of delusion, on account of understanding things as they are.

Tathā paṭhamena aduṭṭho adhivāseti, dutiyena aluddho paṭisevati, tatiyena abhīto parivajjeti, catutthena asammūḷho vinodeti. Paṭhamena nekkhammasukhappatti, itarehi pavivekaupasamasambodhisukhappattiyo hontīti daṭṭhabbā. Tathā vivekajapītisukhasamādhijapītisukhaapītijakāyasukhasatipārisuddhija- upekkhāsukhappattiyo etehi catūhi yathākkamaṃ honti. Evamanekaguṇānubandhehi [P 0.0326] catūhi adhiṭṭhānehi sabbapāramisamūhasaṅgaho veditabbo. Yathā ca catūhi adhiṭṭhānehi sabbapāramisaṅgaho, evaṃ karuṇāpaññāhipīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sabbopi hi bodhisambhāro karuṇāpaññāhi saṅgahito. Karuṇāpaññāpariggahitā hi dānādiguṇā mahābodhisambhārā bhavanti buddhattasiddhipariyosānāti. Evametāsaṃ saṅgaho veditabbo.

Thus, by the first, being unmalicious, one endures; by the second, being ungreedy, one makes use of; by the third, being unafraid, one avoids; by the fourth, being undeluded, one dispels. By the first, there is the attainment of the bliss of renunciation; the others are to be understood as the attainments of the bliss of seclusion, tranquility, and enlightenment. Similarly, the attainments of the bliss of rapture born of seclusion, the bliss of rapture born of concentration, the bodily bliss free from rapture, and the bliss of equanimity born of purified mindfulness—these occur in sequence through these four. Thus, the inclusion of all perfections is to be understood through these four resolutions, which are connected with many qualities. And just as the inclusion of all perfections is by these four resolutions, so too it is to be understood as being by compassion and wisdom. For the entire accumulation for enlightenment is indeed included in compassion and wisdom. Indeed, qualities such as generosity, when embraced by compassion and wisdom, become the great accumulations for enlightenment, culminating in the attainment of Buddhahood. Thus, their inclusion is to be understood in this way.

Ko sampādanūpāyoti? Sakalassāpi puññādisambhārassa sammāsambodhiṃ uddissa anavasesasambharaṇaṃ avekallakāritāyogena, tattha ca sakkaccakāritā ādarabahumānayogena, sātaccakāritā nirantarayogena, cirakālādiyogo ca antarā avosānāpajjanenāti. Taṃ panassa kālaparimāṇaṃ parato āvi bhavissati. Iti caturaṅgayogo etāsaṃ pāramīnaṃ sampādanūpāyo. Tathā mahāsattena bodhāya paṭipajjantena sammāsambodhāya buddhānaṃ puretarameva attā [V 0.0295] niyyātetabbo – “imāhaṃ attabhāvaṃ buddhānaṃ niyyātemī”ti. Taṃtaṃpariggahavatthuñca paṭilābhato puretarameva dānamukhe nissajjitabbaṃ. “Yaṃ kiñci mayhaṃ uppajjanakaṃ jīvitaparikkhārajātaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ sati yācake dassāmi, tesaṃ pana dinnāvasesaṃ eva mayā paribhuñjitabba”nti.

What is the means of accomplishment? The gathering, without remainder, of the entire accumulation of merit and so forth, aiming at perfect enlightenment, through the practice of completeness; and therein, the practice of thoroughness is through the application of respect and high regard; the practice of perseverance is through uninterrupted application; and the practice of long duration is through not giving up in the interim. The measure of this time, however, will become clear later. Thus, this four-factored practice is the means of accomplishing these perfections. Furthermore, a Great Being practicing for enlightenment, for perfect enlightenment, should dedicate himself to the Buddhas before all else, saying: 'I dedicate this very existence to the Buddhas.' And whatever object of possession is obtained, it should be relinquished through the portal of giving before all else, resolving: 'Whatever requisites for life arise for me, I will give all of that to any supplicant who is present; only what remains after giving should be used by me.'

Evaṃ [M 0.0318] hissa sammadeva pariccāgāya kate cittābhisaṅkhāre yaṃ uppajjati pariggahavatthu aviññāṇakaṃ saviññāṇakaṃ vā, tattha ye ime pubbe dāne akataparicayo, pariggahavatthussa parittabhāvo, uḷāramanuññatā, parikkhayacintāti cattāro dānavinibandhā, tesu yadā mahābodhisattassa saṃvijjamānesu deyyadhammesu paccupaṭṭhite ca yācakajane dāne cittaṃ na pakkhandati na kamati. Tena niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ “addhāhaṃ dāne pubbe akataparicayo, tena me etarahi dātukamyatā citte na saṇṭhātī”ti. So evaṃ me ito paraṃ dānābhirataṃ cittaṃ bhavissati, handāhaṃ ito paṭṭhāya dānaṃ dassāmi, nanu mayā paṭikacceva pariggahavatthu yācakānaṃ pariccattanti dānaṃ deti muttacāgo payatapāṇī vosaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Evaṃ mahāsattassa paṭhamo dānavinibandho hato hoti vihato samucchinno.

Thus, when the mental formation is rightly made for relinquishment, whatever object of possession arises—whether inanimate or animate—there are these four hindrances to giving: lack of familiarity with giving in the past, the limited nature of the object of possession, its great desirability, and the thought of its depletion. Among these, when suitable gifts are available and supplicants are present, if the mind of the Great Being does not leap forward or incline toward giving, it should be concluded: 'Surely, I have no prior familiarity with giving, which is why the desire to give does not settle in my mind now.' He then resolves: 'From now on, my mind shall delight in giving. Come, let me begin giving. Have I not already relinquished the object of possession to supplicants beforehand?' Thus, he gives with an open hand, delighting in relinquishment, devoted to charity, accessible to requests, and rejoicing in sharing gifts. In this way, the Great Being's first hindrance to giving is struck down, destroyed, and completely eradicated.

Tathā mahāsatto deyyadhammassa parittabhāve sati vekalle ca iti paṭisañcikkhati – “ahaṃ kho pubbe adānasīlatāya etarahi evaṃ paccayavikalo jāto[P 0.0327], tasmā idāni mayā parittena vā hīnena vā yathāladdhena deyyadhammena attānaṃ pīḷetvāpi dānameva dātabbaṃ, yenāhaṃ āyatimpi dānapāramiṃ matthakaṃ pāpessāmī”ti. So itarītarena taṃ dānaṃ deti muttacāgo payatapāṇī vosaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Evaṃ mahāsattassa dutiyo dānavinibandho hato hoti vihato samucchinno.

Thus, the Great Being reflects when the gift to be given is scarce and deficient: 'In the past, due to my habit of not giving, I have now become so deficient in requisites. Therefore, even by afflicting myself, I must now give whatever small or inferior gift I have obtained, so that in the future I may bring the perfection of giving to its pinnacle.' So he gives that gift, of one kind or another—with an open hand, delighting in relinquishment, devoted to charity, accessible to requests, and rejoicing in sharing gifts. In this way, the Great Being's second hindrance to giving is struck down, destroyed, and completely eradicated.

Tathā mahāsatto deyyadhammassa uḷāramanuññatāya adātukamyatācitte uppajjamāne iti paṭisañcikkhati – “nanu tayā sappurisa uḷāratamā sabbaseṭṭhā sammāsambodhi abhipatthitā, tasmā tadatthaṃ tayā uḷāramanuññe eva deyyadhamme dātuṃ yuttarūpa”nti. So uḷāraṃ manuññañca deti muttacāgo payatapāṇī vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Evaṃ mahāpurisassa tatiyo dānavinibandho hato hoti vihato samucchinno.

Thus, when the thought of unwillingness to give arises in the Great Being's mind because of the magnificent and delightful nature of the gift, he reflects thus: 'Good man, have you not aspired to the most magnificent, supreme perfect enlightenment? Therefore, for that purpose, it is fitting that you give gifts that are magnificent and delightful.' Thus, he gives what is magnificent and delightful—with an open hand, delighting in relinquishment, devoted to charity, accessible to requests, and rejoicing in sharing gifts. In this way, the Great Being's third hindrance to giving is struck down, destroyed, and completely eradicated.

Tathā mahāsatto dānaṃ dento yadā deyyadhammassa parikkhayaṃ passati, so iti paṭisañcikkhati – “ayaṃ kho bhogānaṃ sabhāvo, yadidaṃ khayadhammatā vayadhammatā ca. Api ca [V 0.0296] me pubbe tādisassa dānassa akatattā evaṃ bhogānaṃ parikkhayo dissati, handāhaṃ yathāladdhena deyyadhammena [M 0.0319] parittena vā vipulena vā dānameva dadeyyaṃ, yenāhaṃ āyatiṃ dānapāramiyā matthakaṃ pāpuṇissāmī”ti. So yathāladdhena dānaṃ deti muttacāgo payatapāṇī vosaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Evaṃ mahāsattassa catuttho dānavinibandho hato hoti vihato samucchinno. Evaṃ ye ye dānapāramiyā vinibandhabhūtā anatthā, tesaṃ tesaṃ yathārahaṃ paccavekkhitvā paṭivinodanaṃ upāyo. Yathā ca dānapāramiyā, evaṃ sīlapāramiādīsupi daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Thus, when the Great Being, while giving a gift, sees the depletion of the things to be given, he reflects thus: "This is indeed the nature of possessions—that they are subject to decline and disappearance. Moreover, because of my not giving such gifts before, the depletion of my possessions is now seen. Come, let me give a gift with whatever is obtained, be it little or abundant, so that in the future I may reach the summit of the perfection of giving." So he gives a gift according to what he has obtained—freely giving, with hands outstretched, delighting in relinquishment, accessible to requests, and rejoicing in sharing gifts. In this way, the Great Being's fourth bond to giving is struck down, destroyed, and completely eradicated. Thus, for whatever unprofitable things become bonds to the perfection of giving, the means to dispel them is to consider them appropriately. And as with the perfection of giving, so too should it be understood with the perfection of virtue and the others.

Api ca yaṃ mahāsattassa buddhānaṃ attasanniyyātanaṃ, taṃ sammadeva sabbapāramīnaṃ sampādanūpāyo. Buddhānañhi attānaṃ niyyātetvā ṭhito mahāpuriso tattha tattha bodhisambhārapāripūriyā ghaṭento vāyamanto sarīrassa sukhūpakaraṇānañca upacchedakesu dussahesupi kicchesu durabhisambhavesupi sattasaṅkhārasamupanītesu anatthesu tibbesu pāṇaharesu “ayaṃ mayā attabhāvo buddhānaṃ pariccatto, yaṃ vā taṃ vā ettha hotū”ti taṃnimittaṃ na kampati na vedhati, īsakampi aññathattaṃ na gacchati, kusalārambhe [P 0.0328] aññadatthu acalādhiṭṭhānova hoti, evaṃ attasanniyyātanampi etāsaṃ sampādanūpāyo.

Moreover, the Great Being’s dedication of himself to the Buddhas is indeed the proper means for perfecting all the perfections. For the great man, having dedicated himself to the Buddhas, striving and exerting himself in every way to complete the accumulation of the requisites of enlightenment, even in the face of severe hardships—painful, unbearable, difficult to overcome, and life-threatening, brought about by the actions of beings—does not waver or tremble, thinking, “This body of mine has been offered to the Buddhas; let whatever happens here happen.” He does not deviate even slightly, but rather remains with unshakeable determination in undertaking wholesome actions. Thus, the dedication of oneself is also a means for perfecting these perfections.

Api ca samāsato katābhinīhārassa attani sinehassa parisosanaṃ paresu ca sinehassa parivaḍḍhanaṃ etāsaṃ sampādanūpāyo. Sammāsambodhisamadhigamāya hi katamahāpaṇidhānassa mahāsattassa yāthāvato parijānanena sabbesu dhammesu anupalittassa attani sineho parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gacchati, mahākaruṇāsamāsevanena pana piyaputte viya sabbasatte sampassamānassa tesu mettākaruṇāsineho parivaḍḍhati, tato ca taṃtadavatthānurūpaṃ attaparasantānesu lobhadosamohavigamena vidūrīkatamacchariyādibodhisambhārapaṭipakkho mahāpuriso dānapiyavacanaatthacariyāsamānattatāsaṅkhātehi catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi caturadhiṭṭhānānugatehi accantaṃ janassa saṅgahakaraṇena upari yānattaye avatāraṇaṃ paripācanañca karoti.

Furthermore, in brief, for one who has made the aspiration, the means for accomplishing these perfections is the drying up of affection for oneself and the increase of affection for others. For a Great Being who has made a great vow for the attainment of Perfect Self-Enlightenment, through truly understanding and being unattached to all phenomena, affection for himself comes to an end and exhaustion. But through cultivating great compassion, regarding all beings as like a beloved child, his affection of loving-kindness and compassion for them increases. Consequently, that great man—who, according to the circumstances, has removed greed, hatred, and delusion from his own and others' mental continuums, and who has cast far away stinginess and other opponents of the requisites of enlightenment—by completely gathering people with the four bases of sympathy (namely, giving, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and impartiality), which are accompanied by the four resolutions, brings about their entry into and maturation in the three higher vehicles.

Mahāsattānañhi mahākaruṇā mahāpaññā ca dānena alaṅkatā, dānaṃ piyavacanena, piyavacanaṃ atthacariyāya, atthacariyā samānattatāya alaṅkatā [M 0.0320] saṅgahitā ca. Tesaṃ sabbepi satte attanā nibbisese katvā bodhisambhāresu paṭipajjantānaṃ sabbattha samānasukhadukkhatāya samānattatāya siddhi. Buddhabhūtānampi ca teheva catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi caturadhiṭṭhānaparipūritābhivuddhehi janassa accantikasaṅgahakaraṇena abhivinayanaṃ sijjhati. Dānañhi [V 0.0297] sammāsambuddhānaṃ cāgādhiṭṭhānena paripūritābhivuddhaṃ, piyavacanaṃ saccādhiṭṭhānena, atthacariyā paññādhiṭṭhānena, samānattatā upasamādhiṭṭhānena paripūritābhivuddhā. Tathāgatānañhi sabbasāvakapaccekabuddhehi samānattatā parinibbāne. Tatra hi nesaṃ avisesato ekībhāvo. Tenevāha “natthi vimuttiyā nānatta”nti. Honti cettha –

For Great Beings, great compassion and great wisdom are adorned by giving; giving is adorned by kind speech, kind speech by beneficial conduct, and beneficial conduct by impartiality, and is thereby supported. For them, who treat all beings as no different from themselves while cultivating the requisites of enlightenment, success is achieved through impartiality, which is to experience joy and sorrow as the same everywhere. Even for those who have become Buddhas, the complete guidance of people is accomplished by these same four bases of sympathy, which are perfected and increased by the four resolutions. For the Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones, generosity is perfected and increased by the resolution of relinquishment, kind speech by the resolution of truth, beneficial conduct by the resolution of wisdom, and impartiality by the resolution of peace. For the Tathāgatas, too, there is impartiality with all their disciples and Paccekabuddhas in parinibbāna. For there, their oneness is without distinction. Therefore, it is said: “There is no difference in liberation.” And here are these verses:

“Sacco cāgī upasanto, paññavā anukampako;

Sambhatasabbasambhāro, kaṃ nāmatthaṃ na sādhaye.

"Truthful, generous, peaceful, wise, compassionate, having accumulated all requisites—what aim would such a one not accomplish?"

“Mahākāruṇiko satthā, hitesī ca upekkhako;

Nirapekkho ca sabbattha, aho acchariyo jino.

"The Teacher is greatly compassionate, a well-wisher and equanimous; unattached in all things—oh, how wonderful is the Conqueror!"

“Viratto sabbadhammesu, sattesu ca upekkhako;

Sadā [P 0.0329] sattahite yutto, aho acchariyo jino.

"Dispassionate towards all phenomena, and equanimous towards beings; always engaged in the welfare of beings—oh, how wonderful is the Conqueror!"

“Sabbadā sabbasattānaṃ, hitāya ca sukhāya ca;

Uyyutto akilāsū ca, aho acchariyo jino”ti.

"Always for the welfare and happiness of all beings, striving and without weariness—oh, how wonderful is the Conqueror!"

Kittakena kālena sampādananti? Heṭṭhimena tāva paricchedena cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni mahākappānaṃ satasahassañca, majjhimena aṭṭha asaṅkhyeyyāni mahākappānaṃ satasahassañca, uparimena pana soḷasa asaṅkhyeyyāni mahākappānaṃ satasahassañca. Ete ca bhedā yathākkamaṃ paññādhikasaddhādhikavīriyādhikavasena ñātabbā. Paññādhikānañhi saddhā mandā hoti paññā tikkhā, saddhādhikānaṃ paññā majjhimā hoti, vīriyādhikānaṃ paññā mandā, paññānubhāvena ca sammāsambodhi adhigantabbāti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ.

By how much time is it accomplished? By the lower reckoning, four incalculable ages and one hundred thousand great aeons; by the middle reckoning, eight incalculable ages and one hundred thousand great aeons; and by the higher reckoning, sixteen incalculable ages and one hundred thousand great aeons. These distinctions should be understood respectively as pertaining to those with wisdom predominant, faith predominant, and energy predominant. For those with wisdom predominant, faith is weak and wisdom is sharp; for those with faith predominant, wisdom is moderate; for those with energy predominant, wisdom is weak. It is stated in the commentary that Perfect Self-Enlightenment is to be attained through the power of wisdom.

Apare pana “vīriyassa tikkhamajjhimamudubhāvena bodhisattānaṃ ayaṃ kālavibhāgo”ti vadanti. Avisesena pana vimuttiparipācanīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ tikkhamajjhimamudubhāvena yathāvuttakālabhedena bodhisambhārā tesaṃ pāripūriṃ gacchantīti tayopete kālabhedā yuttātipi vadanti. Evaṃ tividhā [M 0.0321] hi bodhisattā abhinīhārakkhaṇe bhavanti ugghahaṭitaññūvipañcitaññūneyyabhedena. Tesu yo ugghaṭitaññū, so sammāsambuddhassa sammukhā catuppadikaṃ gāthaṃ suṇanto gāthāya tatiyapade apariyosite eva chahi abhiññāhi saha paṭisambhidāhi [V 0.0298] arahattaṃ adhigantuṃ samatthūpanissayo hoti, sace sāvakabodhiyaṃ adhimutto siyā.

Others say, “This division of time for Bodhisattvas is based on the sharp, moderate, or mild nature of their energy.” But generally, they also say that these three divisions of time are appropriate because the Bodhisattvas' requisites for enlightenment reach fulfillment according to the aforementioned divisions of time, through the sharp, moderate, or mild nature of the qualities conducive to the ripening of liberation. Indeed, Bodhisattvas are of three kinds at the moment of their aspiration, distinguished as those of quick understanding, those of elaborated understanding, and those who need guidance. Among them, one of quick understanding, while hearing a four-lined verse in the presence of a Perfectly Self-Enlightened Buddha, has the supporting conditions to attain arahantship along with the six higher knowledges and the analytical knowledges even before the third line of the verse is completed, if he were intent on the enlightenment of a disciple.

Dutiyo bhagavato sammukhā catuppadikaṃ gāthaṃ suṇanto apariyosite eva gāthāya catutthapade chahi abhiññāhi arahattaṃ adhigantuṃ samatthūpanissayo hoti, yadi sāvakabodhiyaṃ adhimutto siyā.

The second, while hearing a four-lined verse in the presence of the Blessed One, has the supporting conditions to attain arahantship with the six higher knowledges even before the fourth line of the verse is completed, if he were intent on the enlightenment of a disciple.

Itaro pana bhagavato sammukhā catuppadikaṃ gāthaṃ sutvā pariyositāya gāthāya chahi abhiññāhi arahattaṃ pattuṃ samatthūpanissayo hoti.

The other, however, having heard a four-lined verse in the presence of the Blessed One, has the supporting conditions to attain arahantship with the six higher knowledges when the verse is completed.

Tayopete vinā kālabhedena katābhinīhāro buddhānaṃ santike laddhabyākaraṇā ca anukkamena pāramiyo paripūrentā yathākkamaṃ yathāvuttabhedena kālena sammāsambodhiṃ pāpuṇanti. Tesu tesu pana kālabhedesu aparipuṇṇesu te [P 0.0330] te mahāsattā divase divase vessantaradānasadisaṃ mahādānaṃ dentāpi tadanurūpe sīlādisabbapāramidhamme ācinantāpi pañca mahāpariccāge pariccajantāpi ñātatthacariyā lokatthacariyā buddhatthacariyā paramakoṭiṃ pāpentāpi antarā ca sammāsambuddhā bhavissantīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Kasmā? Ñāṇassa aparipaccanato buddhakārakadhammānaṃ apariniṭṭhānato. Paricchinnakālanipphāditaṃ viya hi sassaṃ yathāvuttakālaparicchedena parinipphāditā sammāsambodhi tadanantarā sabbussāhena vāyamantenāpi na sakkā adhigantunti pāramipāripūri yathāvuttakālavisesena sampajjatīti veditabbaṃ.

These three, having made their aspiration and having received predictions in the presence of Buddhas, gradually fulfill the perfections and attain Perfect Self-Enlightenment in due order, according to the aforementioned divisions of time. But during those various periods of time when they are incomplete, even though those Great Beings give great gifts daily, like the giving of Vessantara, even though they accumulate all the perfection-qualities such as morality in accordance with that, even though they renounce the five great renunciations, even though they bring the conduct beneficial to relatives, the conduct beneficial to the world, and the conduct for Buddhahood to the highest point—still, the possibility that they will become Perfectly Self-Enlightened Buddhas in the interim does not exist. Why? Because their knowledge is not fully ripened, and the qualities that make a Buddha are not completely fulfilled. For just as a crop produced within a limited time is brought to completion, so Perfect Self-Enlightenment is brought to completion within the stated time limit; it cannot be attained by striving with all effort just before that time. Thus, it should be understood that the complete fulfillment of the perfections is accomplished according to the specific, aforementioned time.

Ko ānisaṃsoti? Ye te katābhinīhārānaṃ bodhisattānaṃ –

What is the benefit? For those Bodhisattvas who have made their aspiration—

“Evaṃ sabbaṅgasampannā, bodhiyā niyatā narā;

Saṃsaraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ, kappakoṭisatehipi.

“Thus, endowed with all qualities, these beings, destined for enlightenment, wander through the long course of saṃsāra, even for billions of eons.”

“Avīcimhi nuppajjanti, tathā lokantaresu ca;

Nijjhāmataṇhā khuppipāsā, na honti kālakañjikā.

“They are not born in Avīci, nor in the Lokantara hells; they are not beings afflicted by burning craving or by hunger and thirst, nor do they become Kālakañjikas.”

“Na [M 0.0322] honti khuddakā pāṇā, upapajjantāpi duggatiṃ;

Jāyamānā manussesu, jaccandhā na bhavanti te.

“They do not become small creatures, even when reborn in a woeful state; when born among humans, they are not born blind.”

“Sotavekallatā [V 0.0299] natthi, na bhavanti mūgapakkhikā;

Itthibhāvaṃ na gacchanti, ubhatobyañjanapaṇḍakā.

“There is no defect of hearing; they do not become mute or crippled; they do not attain the state of a woman, nor become hermaphrodites or eunuchs.”

“Na bhavanti pariyāpannā, bodhiyā niyatā narā;

Muttā ānantarikehi, sabbattha suddhagocarā.

“These beings, destined for enlightenment, do not become subject to such states; freed from the acts of immediate retribution, everywhere their range is pure.”

“Micchādiṭṭhiṃ na sevanti, kammakiriyadassanā;

Vasamānāpi saggesu, asaññaṃ nūpapajjare.

“They do not cultivate wrong view, being those who see kamma and its result; even while dwelling in heavenly realms, they are not reborn in the realm of non-perception.”

“Suddhāvāsesu devesu, hetu nāma na vijjati;

Nekkhammaninnā sappurisā, visaṃyuttā bhavābhave;

Caranti lokatthacariyāyo, pūrenti sabbapāramī”ti. (dha. sa. aṭṭha. nidānakathā; jā. aṭṭha. 1.dūrenidānakathā; apa. aṭṭha. 1.dūrenidānakathā) –

“For them, no cause for rebirth among the gods of the Pure Abodes is found; these good persons are inclined to renunciation, detached from existence and non-existence; they practice for the world's benefit, fulfilling all perfections.”

Evaṃ saṃvaṇṇitā ānisaṃsā. Ye ca “sato sampajāno, ānanda, bodhisatto tusitā kāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkamatī”tiādinā (ma. ni. 3.200; dī. ni. 2.17) soḷasa acchariyabbhutadhammappakārā, ye ca “sītaṃ byapagataṃ hoti, uṇhañca upasammatī”tiādinā (bu. vaṃ. 2.83) “jāyamāne kho, sāriputta, bodhisatte ayaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhatī”tiādinā (ma. ni. 3.201; dī. ni. 2.32) ca dvattiṃsa pubbanimittappakārā, ye vā panaññepi [P 0.0331] bodhisattānaṃ adhippāyasamijjhanaṃ kammādīsu vasībhāvoti evamādayo tattha tattha jātakabuddhavaṃsādīsu dassitākārā ānisaṃsā, te sabbepi etāsaṃ ānisaṃsā. Tathā yathānidassitabhedā alobhādosādiguṇayugalādayo cāti veditabbā.

Such are the benefits that have been described. Those sixteen kinds of amazing and wonderful phenomena, such as “Mindful and clearly comprehending, Ānanda, the Bodhisatta, passing away from the Tusita realm, enters his mother’s womb,” and so on (Majjhima Nikāya 3.200; Dīgha Nikāya 2.17); those thirty-two kinds of preliminary signs, such as “The cold disappears, and the heat subsides,” and so on (Buddhavaṃsa 2.83), and “When the Bodhisatta is born, Sāriputta, this ten-thousandfold world-system trembles, shakes, and quakes,” and so on (Majjhima Nikāya 3.201; Dīgha Nikāya 2.32); or even other benefits, such as the fulfillment of the Bodhisattas’ intentions, mastery over kamma, and so forth, benefits of such a kind that are shown here and there in the Jātakas, Buddhavaṃsa, and other texts—all these are their benefits. And also, pairs of qualities such as non-greed and non-hatred, and so on, according to the distinctions shown, should be understood to be their benefits.

Api ca yasmā bodhisatto abhinīhārato paṭṭhāya sabbasattānaṃ pitusamo hoti hitesitāya, dakkhiṇeyyako garu bhāvanīyo paramañca puññakkhettaṃ hoti guṇavisesayogena. Yebhuyyena ca manussānaṃ piyo hoti, amanussānaṃ piyo hoti, devatāhi anupālīyati, mettākaruṇāparibhāvitasantānatāya vāḷamigādīhi ca anabhibhavanīyo hoti, yasmiṃ yasmiñca sattanikāye [V 0.0300] paccājāyati, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ uḷārena vaṇṇena uḷārena yasena uḷārena sukhena uḷārena balena uḷārena [M 0.0323] ādhipateyyena aññe satte abhibhavati puññavisesayogato.

Moreover, from the time of his aspiration, the Bodhisatta is like a father to all beings in his wish for their welfare; he is worthy of offerings, revered, worthy of esteem, and the supreme field of merit due to his special qualities. And for the most part, he is dear to humans, dear to non-humans, protected by deities, and unconquerable by wild beasts and the like due to his mind being imbued with loving-kindness and compassion. In whatever group of beings he is reborn, he surpasses other beings with outstanding beauty, outstanding fame, outstanding happiness, outstanding strength, and outstanding sovereignty, due to his special merit.

Appābādho hoti appātaṅko, suvisuddhā cassa saddhā hoti suvisadā, suvisuddhaṃ vīriyaṃ, satisamādhipaññā suvisadā, mandakileso hoti mandadaratho mandapariḷāho, kilesānaṃ mandabhāveneva suvaco hoti padakkhiṇaggāhī, khamo hoti sorato, sakhilo hoti paṭisanthārakusalo, akkodhano hoti anupanāhī, amakkhī hoti apaḷāsī, anissukī hoti amaccharī, asaṭho hoti amāyāvī, athaddho hoti anatimānī, asāraddho hoti appamatto, parato upatāpasaho hoti paresaṃ anupatāpī, yasmiñca gāmakhette paṭivasati, tattha sattānaṃ bhayādayo upaddavā yebhuyyena anuppannā nuppajjanti, uppannā ca vūpasammanti, yesu ca apāyesu uppajjati, na tattha pacurajano viya dukkhena adhimattaṃ pīḷīyati, bhiyyosomattāya saṃvegamāpajjati. Tasmā mahāpurisassa yathārahaṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ bhave labbhamānā ete sattānaṃ pitusamatādakkhiṇeyyatādayo guṇavisesā ānisaṃsāti veditabbā.

He is free from illness and disease. His faith is very pure and bright. His energy is very pure. His mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom are very bright. He has few defilements, little anxiety, and little torment. Because his defilements are few, he is easy to instruct, readily receptive, patient, gentle, friendly, and skilled in cordiality. He is free from anger and resentment, free from contempt and rivalry, free from envy and selfishness, free from dishonesty and deceptiveness, free from stubbornness and conceit, free from impetuosity and negligence. He is tolerant of oppression from others without oppressing them. In whatever village or field he dwells, the fears and troubles of beings there mostly do not arise, and if they do arise, they subside. Even if he is born in the woeful states, he is not afflicted excessively with suffering like most people, but rather attains a greater sense of urgency. Therefore, it should be understood that these special qualities—such as being like a father to beings and being worthy of offerings—are the benefits that a great being obtains as is appropriate in each and every existence.

Tathā āyusampadā rūpasampadā kulasampadā issariyasampadā ādeyyavacanatā mahānubhāvatāti etepi mahāpurisassa pāramīnaṃ ānisaṃsāti veditabbā. Tattha āyusampadā nāma tassaṃ tassaṃ upapattiyaṃ dīghāyukatā ciraṭṭhitikatā, tāya yathāraddhāni kusalasamādānāni pariyosāpeti, bahuñca kusalaṃ upacinoti. Rūpasampadā nāma [P 0.0332] abhirūpatā dassanīyatā pāsādikatā, tāya rūpappamāṇānaṃ sattānaṃ pasādāvaho hoti sambhāvanīyo. Kulasampadā nāma uḷāresu kulesu abhinibbatti, tāya jātimadādimadamattānampi upasaṅkamanīyo hoti payirupāsanīyo, tena te nibbisevane karoti. Issariyasampadā nāma mahāvibhavatā mahesakkhatā mahāparivāratā ca, tāhi saṅgaṇhitabbe catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi saṅgaṇhituṃ, niggahetabbe dhammena niggahetuñca samattho hoti.

Thus, the accomplishment of long life, the accomplishment of beauty, the accomplishment of noble birth, the accomplishment of sovereignty, having weighty speech, and great power—these too should be understood as the benefits of a great being’s perfections. Herein, the accomplishment of long life means longevity and enduring existence in each rebirth. By this, one completes the virtuous undertakings one has begun and accumulates much merit. The accomplishment of beauty means being handsome, pleasant to see, and inspiring. By this, one inspires confidence in beings who judge by physical appearance and becomes worthy of respect. The accomplishment of noble birth means being reborn in illustrious families. By this, one becomes worthy of approach and veneration even by those who are intoxicated with pride of birth, and thus one brings them to attend upon him. The accomplishment of sovereignty means great wealth, high status, and a large retinue. With these, one is capable of supporting those who should be supported through the four bases of benevolence and of restraining those who should be restrained righteously.

Ādeyyavacanatā nāma saddheyyatā paccayikatā, tāya sattānaṃ pamāṇabhūto hoti, alaṅghanīyā cassa āṇā hoti. Mahānubhāvatā nāma ānubhāvamahantatā, tāya parehi na abhibhūyati, sayameva [M 0.0324] pana pare aññadatthu abhibhavati dhammena samena yathābhūtaguṇehi ca, evamete āyusampadādayo mahāpurisassa pāramīnaṃ ānisaṃsā, sayañca aparimāṇassa puññasambhārassa parivuḍḍhihetubhūtā yānattaye sattānaṃ avatāraṇassa paripācanassa ca kāraṇabhūtāti veditabbā.

Having weighty speech means being trustworthy and reliable. Through that, one becomes a standard for beings, and one's command is inviolable. Great power means the greatness of one’s power. Through that, one is not overcome by others, but rather, for the benefit of others, one overcomes them by means of righteousness, impartiality, and genuine qualities. Thus, these accomplishments, beginning with that of long life, are the benefits of the perfections of a great being. And they should be understood as being themselves a cause for the growth of an immeasurable accumulation of merit, and as a cause for leading beings into the three vehicles and for their maturation.

Kiṃ [V 0.0301] phalanti? Samāsato tāva sammāsambuddhabhāvo etāsaṃ phalaṃ, vitthārato pana dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇaasītianubyañjanabyāmappabhādianekaguṇagaṇasamujjalarūpakāyasampatti- adhiṭṭhānasabalacatuvesārajjachaasādhāraṇañāṇaaṭṭhārasāveṇika- buddhadhammappabhutianantāparimāṇa guṇasamudayopasobhinī dhammakāyasirī. Yāvatā pana buddhaguṇā ye anekehipi kappehi sammāsambuddhenāpi vācāya pariyosāpetuṃ na sakkā, idametāsaṃ phalaṃ. Vuttañcetaṃ –

What is their fruit? In brief, the state of a perfectly enlightened Buddha is their fruit. In detail, it is the attainment of a physical body resplendent with the thirty-two marks of a great man, the eighty minor characteristics, a fathom-wide radiant aura, and a multitude of other excellent qualities; and it is the glory of the Dhamma-body, adorned with an infinite and immeasurable collection of virtues, such as the four kinds of intrepidity strengthened by the power of determination, the six kinds of uncommon knowledge, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and so forth. Indeed, whatever virtues of a Buddha there are, which even a perfectly enlightened Buddha could not fully describe in words over many eons—this is their fruit. And it has been said:

“Buddhopi buddhassa bhaṇeyya vaṇṇaṃ, kappampi ce aññamabhāsamāno;

Khīyetha kappo ciradīghamantare, vaṇṇo na khīyetha tathāgatassā”ti. (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.304; 3.141; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.425; udā. aṭṭha. 53; cariyā. aṭṭha. nidānakathā);

“Even a Buddha, speaking the praise of a Buddha for an entire eon without uttering another word; that eon would come to an end in the long lapse of time, but the praise of the Tathāgata would not come to an end.”

Evamettha pāramīsu pakiṇṇakakathā veditabbā.

Thus, the miscellaneous discourse on the perfections should be understood here.

Yaṃ pana pāḷiyaṃ “datvā dātabbakaṃ dāna”ntiādinā sabbāpi pāramī ekajjhaṃ dassetvā parato “kosajjaṃ bhayato disvā”tiādinā pariyosānagāthādvayaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ [P 0.0333] yehi vīriyārambhamettābhāvanā appamādavihārehi yathāvuttā buddhakārakadhammā visadabhāvaṃ gatā sammāsambodhisaṅkhātā ca attano vimutti paripācitā, tehi veneyyānampi vimuttiparipācanāya ovādadānatthaṃ vutthaṃ.

Now, in the Pāli text, after all the perfections have been shown together with the words, “Having given a gift that should be given,” and so forth, thereafter two concluding verses are spoken, beginning, “Seeing laziness as a danger.” These were spoken by those in whom the aforesaid qualities that make a Buddha—such as the undertaking of energy, the cultivation of loving-kindness, and abiding in diligence—have reached a state of clarity, and whose own liberation, known as perfect enlightenment, has been brought to maturity. They were spoken by them for the purpose of giving an exhortation for the maturing of the liberation of those to be trained.

Tattha kosajjaṃ bhayato disvā, vīriyārambhañca khematoti iminā paṭipakkhe ādīnavadassanamukhena vīriyārambhe ānisaṃsaṃ dasseti. Āraddhavīriyā hothāti iminā vīriyārambhe niyojeti. Yasmā ca –

Therein, with the words, “Seeing laziness as a danger, and the undertaking of energy as safety,” he shows the benefit in undertaking energy by way of showing the danger in its opposite. With the words, “Be resolute in energy,” he enjoins the undertaking of energy. And because—

“Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṃ, kusalassa upasampadā;

Sacittapariyodapanaṃ, etaṃ buddhāna sāsana”nti. (dha. pa. 183; dī. ni. 2.90; netti. 30, 50) –

“The non-doing of all evil, the undertaking of the wholesome, the purification of one’s own mind—this is the teaching of the Buddhas.”

Saṅkhepato[M 0.0325]. Vitthārato pana sakalena buddhavacanena pakāsitā sabbāpi sampattiyo ekanteneva sammappadhānādhīnā, tasmā bhagavā vīriyārambhe niyojetvā “esā buddhānusāsanī”ti āha.
